name: London Lowball
description: London Lowball is a specific variant of Seven Card Stud played for the 'Low' hand, essentially similar to Razz but traditionally played in London card rooms with Pot-Limit or Spread-Limit structures. The goal is to make the worst possible five-card poker hand out of seven cards dealt. In London rules, the Ace is always low, and straights and flushes do not count against the player, making A-2-3-4-5 the 'nuts' (best possible hand).

history.origins: Developed in the 1970s and 80s in London gaming clubs like the Victoria Casino ('The Vic'). It adapted American Razz rules to the British preference for Pot-Limit betting.
timeline: 1980s: Becomes a staple in London's high-stakes poker circuit.
1990s: Differentiated from US Razz by the prevalence of Pot-Limit betting instead of Fixed-Limit.
2000s: Gained international recognition through the Late Night Poker television show.
Present: Still played in European mixed-games rotation (H.O.R.S.E. or similar).
history.cultural: In the UK, it is often called 'London Razz'.
history.evolution: The game moved from a 'side-show' in Stud circles to a primary game for 'action' players who enjoy the mathematical complexity of drawing to low hands.

setup.dealing: Two cards face-down, one card face-up to begin. Subsequent rounds follow the 7-card stud pattern (4th, 5th, 6th streets up, 7th street down).
setup.equipment: Standard deck, poker chips, dealer button.

rules.objective: Form the lowest possible 5-card hand. Straights and Flushes ARE NOT counted (California/A-5 Lowball rules).
rules.gameplay: 1. **Bring-In**: The player with the HIGHEST door card (1st up card) must pay a mandatory bring-in bet. 2. **Betting Rounds**: Five rounds of betting (starting after 3rd street). 3. **Showdown**: Players reveal 7 cards; best 5-card 'Low' hand wins.
keyRules: Ace-to-Five lowball ranking: A-2-3-4-5 (Wheel) is best hand.
Straights and flushes do not count against player.
Highest door card pays bring-in (Ace is low, so King is worst).
Pairs are badâ€”any no-pair hand beats any paired hand.
Compare highest cards first when ranking hands.

strategy.basic: Starting Hand Selection: Only play if your first three cards are both 8 or lower with no pair. If your hole card is paired with your upcard, or if you show a high card like a King or Queen, strongly consider folding.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Hidden' Low: If your two hole cards are an A and a 2, and your up-card is a Jack, your hand looks weak to opponents. Use this to induce bluffs from players with 'cleaner' 3rd-street up-cards.
strategy.advanced: Pot-Limit Pressure: Since it's Pot-Limit, if you have a lock on the low (e.g., you show 3-4-5-6 and hold an Ace), bet the maximum to force opponents who have 5-6-7-8 to either pay a premium or fold their second-best draws.
tips: In Lowball, the Ace is your most valuable card. If you see three Aces showing among your opponents' up-cards, your own Ace-high draw becomes much stronger (as they are less likely to have an Ace in the hole).
Don't chase a 9-low if the pot is large and your opponent is showing the potential for a 7-low. You are 'drawing dead' in many scenarios.
